description: Replace the churn-prone equality-shaped passFloor maintenance with a guarded minimum-headroom rule inside the gate that already measures, and re-record both lanes from real branch measurements.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Confirms the two Bun behaviours every oracle in this PRD depends on: --test-name-pattern / -t is documented as 'Run only tests with a name that matches the given regex' (so parentheses in a test name break a -t filter, which is why every -t oracle here uses a parenthesis-free substring), and the summary block that check-skip-ratchet.ts parses is ' N pass' / ' N fail' plus the 'Ran N tests across M files. [t]' tally, with the skip line omitted entirely at zero. Under CLAUDECODE=1 Bun hides per-test passing indicators but keeps the summary statistics intact, so the summary-line greps stay valid inside an agent session. No breaking changes or deprecations affecting this gate.

userStories.title: Enforce a guarded MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM in the skip-ratchet gate and re-record the host lane
userStories.description: As the maintainer of the quality spine, I need the gate that already runs the suite to reject a passFloor recorded too close to the observed pass count, with an explicit applicability guard, so that a floor can never be re-recorded at equality and restart the four-cycle churn, and I need the host lane re-recorded from a real branch measurement so the lane file stops asserting a falsifiable pass number.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts exports a doc-commented constant MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM whose value is pinned at 50 (the issue requires at least 50; this PRD pins exactly 50 so the fixture values named below are unambiguous). The doc comment states the anti-churn rationale: adding tests only widens the gap, so the rule fires once, is fixed once, and stays satisfied unless someone re-tightens the floor toward equality. [oracle: grep -q 'export const MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM' scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts && bun -e 'import { MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM as H } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; process.exit(H >= 50 ? 0 : 1)']

checkSuiteRan REJECTS a lane whose recorded passFloor sits less than MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM below the observed pass count, and the rejection message names the too-tight-floor failure mode distinctly: it contains the substring 'too tight' and must NOT contain the existing crashed-run wording 'suite likely crashed', because the two failure modes demand opposite operator responses (re-record the floor lower vs investigate a broken run). SWEPT RED against main on 2026-07-28: this oracle exits 1 today because the gate accepts a floor equal to the observed count. [oracle: bun -e 'import { checkSuiteRan } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const out=" 5758 pass
 0 fail
Ran 5758 tests across 343 files. [1s]
"; const r=checkSuiteRan(out,5758,"host"); process.exit(r!==null && r.ok===false && /too tight/.test(r.message) && !r.message.includes("suite likely crashed") ? 0 : 1)']

APPLICABILITY GUARD (this is the core semantics of the rule and must not be invented at implementation time): the too-tight rejection fires ONLY when the recorded passFloor is greater than 0. A recorded floor of 0 means 'no floor declared' (the pre-existing below-floor comparison is already vacuous at 0, since any observed count is >= 0), so a zero floor is ACCEPTED regardless of how small the observed pass count is; a positive floor whose gap to the observed count is at least MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM is also accepted. Both halves are green on main today and must stay green, which is exactly what leaves the 13 default-floor-0 call sites of fakeExpectations in test/test-in-container.test.ts untouched. [oracle: bun -e 'import { checkSuiteRan } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const out=" 5 pass
 0 fail
 2 skip
Ran 7 tests across 2 files. [0.10s]
"; process.exit(checkSuiteRan(out,0,"container")===null ? 0 : 1)' && bun -e 'import { checkSuiteRan } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const out=" 200 pass
 0 fail
 2 skip
Ran 202 tests across 3 files. [0.10s]
"; process.exit(checkSuiteRan(out,100,"container")===null ? 0 : 1)']

ORDERING PIN: the pre-existing below-the-floor rejection still runs BEFORE the headroom rejection, so an observed pass count that falls below a positive floor keeps reporting the existing 'below recorded passFloor' wording rather than the new too-tight wording. Green on main and must stay green. [oracle: bun -e 'import { checkSuiteRan } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const out=" 0 pass
 0 fail
 3 skip
Ran 3 tests across 1 files. [0.10s]
"; const r=checkSuiteRan(out,5,"container"); process.exit(r!==null && r.message.includes("below recorded") ? 0 : 1)']

CONTRADICTION REPAIR (mandatory: the new rule breaks a currently GREEN test). test/check-skip-ratchet.test.ts:86, whose full name is 'null (suite ran cleanly) when tally line present and pass count clears the floor', feeds fixture floor 5700 against a 5702-pass fixture (gap 2) and must be REPAIRED by giving its fixture real headroom: lower the fixture floor to 5600 against the same 5702-pass output (gap 102). The test must SURVIVE under a name still containing the substring 'pass count clears the floor' and must NOT be deleted; resolving the contradiction by deletion is forbidden. [oracle: out=$(bun test -t 'pass count clears the floor' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ 0 fail']

CONTRADICTION REPAIR, second site inside the same file: the makeExpectations helper in the 'checkSkipRatchet' describe block (test/check-skip-ratchet.test.ts:158-169) records host floor 5700 and container floor 5650 against fixtures of 5702 / 5701 / 5662 pass (gaps 2, 1, 12), all of which the new rule rejects. Lower those fixture floors to host 5600 and container 5550 so every gap clears 50, keeping the deliberately-below-floor fixture (12 pass) still failing on the below-floor branch. [oracle: out=$(bun test -t 'newly introduced skip on the host lane' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ 0 fail']

CONTRADICTION REPAIR, container site: test/test-in-container.test.ts:375 'exits 0 when the completion tally is present and observed pass meets the container passFloor' currently uses fakeExpectations(2, 5) against FIXTURE_ALL_PASS (5 pass), a gap of 0 that the new rule rejects, and it cannot be repaired by widening FIXTURE_ALL_PASS's headroom because a 5-pass fixture can never sit 50 above a non-negative floor. Repair it by adding a new synthetic fixture with exactly 200 pass / 0 fail / 2 skip and a 'Ran 202 tests across 3 files.' tally, driven by fakeExpectations(2, 100), so the test keeps exercising a POSITIVE floor (gap 100) instead of degenerating into the zero-floor no-op path. The other 13 fakeExpectations call sites (lines 292, 301, 310, 319, 331, 341, 354, 397, 416, 430, 445, 456, 465) keep the default floor 0 and need no edit, per the applicability guard above; the whole file must be green. [oracle: out=$(bun test ./test/test-in-container.test.ts 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ 0 fail']

A NEW test pins the too-tight rejection under a stable, parenthesis-free name containing the substring 'floor too tight', asserting both that the result is a failure and that its message does not reuse the crashed-run wording. [oracle: out=$(bun test -t 'floor too tight' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ 0 fail']

A NEW test pins the applicability guard under a stable, parenthesis-free name containing the substring 'floor of 0 disables the headroom rule', asserting that a recorded floor of 0 is accepted even with a tiny observed pass count. [oracle: out=$(bun test -t 'floor of 0 disables the headroom rule' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ 0 fail']

The host lane in test/helpers/lane-expectations.json is re-recorded from a full-PATH `bun test` run executed on THIS branch: passFloor sits at least MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM below the freshly measured pass count (round the floor down to a multiple of 100 so the real gap is >= 200 and the record does not need touching again next cycle), measuredAt is the date of that run, and measuredVia contains that same measuredAt date, the exact command used, and the measured counts in exactly the token form '<N> pass / <M> fail / <K> skip' (host runs at zero skips, so record '0 skip' explicitly even though Bun omits the line). No prose in the object may contradict the numbers recorded in the same object. Do NOT copy 5758 / 5734 / 5731 forward as the new floor: measure again. SWEPT RED against main on 2026-07-28 (the oracle exits 1 today: no token form, measuredVia does not contain measuredAt, measuredAt is the stale 2026-07-27, gap is 27). [oracle: bun -e 'import { MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM as H } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const f=await Bun.file("test/helpers/lane-expectations.json").json(); const l=f.lanes.host; const m=/(\d+) pass \/ (\d+) fail \/ (\d+) skip/.exec(l.measuredVia); const ok=!!m && Number(m[1])-l.passFloor>=H && Number(m[2])===0 && Number(m[3])===l.expectedSkips && l.measuredVia.includes(l.measuredAt) && l.measuredAt>"2026-07-27"; process.exit(ok?0:1)']

expectedSkips is untouched by this story and keeps strict two-directional equality: the headroom rule applies ONLY to passFloor, and the doc comment stating that ANY delta in either direction fails survives in substance. [oracle: grep -q 'ANY delta (increase or decrease)' scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts && out=$(bun test -t 'a decrease also fails and names the negative delta' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ 0 fail']

COST PIN: the gate spine gains no fourth full-suite invocation and no new gate. The headroom check reuses the output scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts already captures at line 224 and must not spawn a suite run of its own; the check-all manifest still declares exactly 14 gates. [oracle: test "$(grep -rn "Bun.spawnSync(\['bun', 'test'" scripts/*.ts | wc -l | tr -d ' ')" = "2" && out=$(bun test -t 'has 14 gates in order' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE '^ 0 fail']

The host-lane ratchet gate is GREEN at the end of this story, and handoff.json records the honest red-then-green order explicitly: landing the rule alone turns `bun scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts` RED on the stale recorded floor (live gap 27 on main), and re-recording the host lane in this same story turns it GREEN. [oracle: bun scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
The full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts (rule + constant, checkSuiteRan at :192-216, the pass-floor branch at :205, the already-captured suite output at :224), test/check-skip-ratchet.test.ts (repairs at :86 and the makeExpectations helper at :158-169, plus the two new tests), test/test-in-container.test.ts (repair at :375 plus the new 200-pass fixture; the fakeExpectations helper is at :41-52), test/helpers/lane-expectations.json (host lane re-record). CORRECTION OF A FALSE PREMISE CARRIED BY THE PREVIOUS PLAN ROUND: it is NOT true unconditionally that 'a container fixture floor of 0 makes a headroom check pass trivially'. Under an UNGUARDED rule, floor 0 against a 5-pass fixture yields a gap of 5 and would be REJECTED, which is precisely why 13 default-floor call sites would have gone red. A zero floor passes only BECAUSE this PRD pins the passFloor > 0 applicability guard (criterion 3); reason from that guard, not from a claim of trivial passing. MEASURED CONTEXT, do not re-derive by guessing: main at 3777652a measures 5758 pass / 0 fail across 343 files in ~135s while the recorded floor is 5731, a live gap of 27, so any headroom >= 28 makes the current record red and 50 is comfortably red; the recorded container floor is 5691 and its gap is expected to be similarly tight, which US-002 fixes. The host measurement this story records is free: you must run the full `bun test` for the gates anyway, so read 'Ran N tests across M files' and ' N pass' off that same run rather than adding a run. NEVER freeze a live-growing count as a comparand (patterns.md derive-don't-freeze rule, patterns.md:932): the 5758/5731/5734/5691 numbers appear here as dated evidence, not as values to embed; fixture literals handed to a pure function inside a self-contained test or oracle are fine, a recorded expectation compared against a growing suite is the defect itself. Every oracle above was executed against unmodified main on 2026-07-28 per the oracle-falsifiability rule (patterns.md:928); re-run each one before trusting it, and note that the oracle-lint's per-clause frozen-comparand scoping (patterns.md:934) is why each derivation and its comparand sit in the same shell clause. `bun test -t` is a REGEX (confirmed against https://bun.sh/docs/cli/test): never reintroduce parentheses into a -t oracle, and never read a run that matched 0 tests as success, which is what the '^ [1-9][0-9]* pass' half of each -t oracle enforces. Related prior art: patterns.md:1098 (a gate parsing subprocess text must demand positive evidence the subprocess completed) is the bullet this gate implements. Never trust prd.json's review.findings array (it has lied in CAM-434, CAM-424 and CAM-448); the truth is scripts/cam/review-report.json under key 'text'. Scratch files go in /tmp, never inside the repo tree.

userStories.title: Re-measure and re-record the container lane from a real Docker run
userStories.description: As the maintainer of the container lane, I need its expectedSkips, passFloor, measuredAt and measuredVia re-recorded from an actual in-container suite run on this branch, so the lane file stops carrying an inferred or stale number and the headroom rule holds on both lanes.
acceptanceCriteria: The container lane in test/helpers/lane-expectations.json is re-recorded from an ACTUAL `bun scripts/test-in-container.ts` run on this branch, never inferred and never derived from the host lane's delta: expectedSkips equals the measured skip count exactly, passFloor sits at least MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM below the measured pass count (round the floor down to a multiple of 100 so the real gap is >= 200), measuredAt is the date of that run, and measuredVia contains that same measuredAt date, the exact command used, and the measured counts in exactly the token form '<N> pass / <M> fail / <K> skip'. SWEPT RED against main on 2026-07-28 (no token form present, measuredVia does not contain measuredAt, measuredAt is the stale 2026-07-27). [oracle: bun -e 'import { MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM as H } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const f=await Bun.file("test/helpers/lane-expectations.json").json(); const l=f.lanes.container; const m=/(\d+) pass \/ (\d+) fail \/ (\d+) skip/.exec(l.measuredVia); const ok=!!m && Number(m[1])-l.passFloor>=H && Number(m[2])===0 && Number(m[3])===l.expectedSkips && l.measuredVia.includes(l.measuredAt) && l.measuredAt>"2026-07-27"; process.exit(ok?0:1)']
The container gate passes end to end on the re-recorded values. [oracle: bun scripts/test-in-container.ts]

If Docker is unavailable when this story runs, the story HALTS and reports the blocker instead of writing any inferred number: an invented container count reproduces the exact fidelity defect this issue exists to remove. Docker was verified UP (29.4.0) on 2026-07-28, so the expected path is a real run. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

INVARIANCE PIN: the host lane record US-001 wrote is untouched by this story and still satisfies its own derived headroom/prose check. [oracle: bun -e 'import { MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM as H } from "./scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts"; const f=await Bun.file("test/helpers/lane-expectations.json").json(); const l=f.lanes.host; const m=/(\d+) pass \/ (\d+) fail \/ (\d+) skip/.exec(l.measuredVia); const ok=!!m && Number(m[1])-l.passFloor>=H && Number(m[2])===0 && Number(m[3])===l.expectedSkips && l.measuredVia.includes(l.measuredAt) && l.measuredAt>"2026-07-27"; process.exit(ok?0:1)']
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
The full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: test/helpers/lane-expectations.json (container object only). The container lane is exercised by scripts/test-in-container.ts, which calls checkSuiteRan(output, containerExpectation.passFloor, 'container') at :238 before the skip comparison, so US-001's rule applies to this lane through the same function; nothing in scripts/ needs editing here. The run wires waivers via `docker exec -e CAM_TEST_WAIVERS=tmux,pgrep,uuidgen` and the default container name is cam-worker. docs/container-test-baseline.md is background for how the skip set was triaged (its own historical 3098/3064 figures are a dated snapshot and are deliberately OUT OF SCOPE for this cycle: do not edit them). The recorded container floor on main is 5691 against a host measurement of 5758, so expect a tight gap and a red gate until this story lands. Do not copy 5691, 5694 or any host-derived arithmetic into the file; the issue forbids exactly that. Same doctrine as US-001: derive-don't-freeze (patterns.md:932), oracle-falsifiability sweep (patterns.md:928), and no frozen live count anywhere in the record beyond the dated prose token. Container-mode dev may need the image up first; if `ensure-up` has to run, that is expected and is not an inferred measurement.

userStories.title: Record the passFloor-headroom convention in patterns.md
userStories.description: As a future spec author, I need the floor-with-headroom convention and its deliberate contrast with expectedSkips written down where agents grep, so nobody re-invents the equality demand and restarts the churn this issue removed.
acceptanceCriteria: scripts/cam/patterns.md gains a bullet stating that passFloor is a floor carrying declared headroom and must never be maintained at equality with the current pass count. Verified ABSENT on main on 2026-07-28 (grep -c returns 0), so this oracle is red now and green when the bullet lands. [oracle: grep -q 'never be maintained at equality' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The same bullet names the enforcing mechanism so a reader can find it: the constant MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM in scripts/check-skip-ratchet.ts, and its applicability guard that a recorded floor of 0 means 'no floor declared' and is not enforced. [oracle: grep -q 'MIN_PASS_FLOOR_HEADROOM' scripts/cam/patterns.md && grep -q 'no floor declared' scripts/cam/patterns.md]

The same bullet records the deliberate contrast (expectedSkips stays exactly equal, because detecting skip drift in either direction is the entire purpose of the ratchet) and the evidence of four measured invalidations (US-006 wrote 5720, US-R1-002 added 11 and staled it, US-R2-001 corrected to 5731, US-R2-002 added 3 and staled it again, then CAM-448 added 27 across PRDs and staled it a fourth time), using the exact phrase 'four measured invalidations'. [oracle: grep -q 'four measured invalidations' scripts/cam/patterns.md && grep -q 'expectedSkips' scripts/cam/patterns.md]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
The full quality spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/cam/patterns.md only (append a bullet; never truncate, never reorder existing bullets). This story is split out from the gate work deliberately: its oracles are independent of the rule change and it must not compete for context with the measurement-heavy stories. patterns.md is large and appending may trip the file-size gate inside `bun run check:all`; raising that file's budget in the same commit is the expected, in-scope resolution (workers raise their own budget), not a reason to shorten the bullet. Do NOT mark the bullet '[resolved YYYY-MM]': this is a living convention, not a one-time mechanic. Numbers in the bullet are historical evidence with dates attached, which is the one legitimate use of a past count; do not phrase them as comparands and do not add any oracle that greps for a live count.
